summary: Command-line options override configuration settings only, not playbook keywords or variables. For single-value options the last one given wins, while some options such as -i accept multiple values that are combined.
questions: Why doesn't my -u flag override the user set in inventory?
What happens if I pass the same command-line flag twice?
Can I pass multiple inventory files with -i?
Do CLI options override playbook keywords?
How can I force a value from the command line to override everything?

answer_card.title: How command-line options rank in precedence
answer_card.answer_md:
Command-line options only override **configuration settings**. They do *not* override playbook keywords, inventory variables or playbook variables.

- For single-value options, the last one wins: `ansible -u mike -m ping myhost -u carol` connects as `carol`.
- Some options accept multiple values and combine them, for example `ansible -i /path/inventory1 -i /path/inventory2 -m ping all`.

To override everything from the command line, pass a variable with `-e`/`--extra-vars` instead (that is variable precedence, not CLI option precedence).
